exits.failMessage: A sealed blast door. The Array's deepest systems lie beyond — but you have no reason to go there. Yet.
A sealed blast door. The Array's deepest systems lie beyond — but you have no reason to go there. Yet.
A massive conduit descends toward the Dayside Spire. The Array Overseer's security field blocks passage — neutralize the facility guardian first.

lines: Deeper. The ceiling is lower here, the heat more oppressive. The hum of machinery is constant — felt in your bones.
The central chamber dominates the space: a massive containment pool filled with a murky green-brown fluid. Pipes feed into it from all directions. Monitoring equipment lines the perimeter.
This isn't a factory. It's a laboratory. The Array is trying to grow something organic.

This isn't a factory. It's a laboratory. The Array is trying to grow something organic.
The central pool is warm. Bubbles rise to its surface at irregular intervals. The fluid smells faintly of soil and ammonia — organic, unmistakably organic.
A monitoring readout nearby displays: 'CULTURE MEDIUM 7-SIGMA-4. COMPOSITION: Synthetic amino acid substrate. TARGET: Chloroplast-analog enzyme. STATUS: Generation 847, Iteration 4,291,006.'
Four million iterations. The Array has been trying to synthesize plant biology for longer than the outpost has existed.

The pieces connect. The Array trades for biological catalysts from the Ring — compounds it cannot manufacture. That trade is humanity's leverage. The reason the Array negotiates instead of dictates.
But this facility exists to change that equation. If the Array can synthesize its own biological compounds, it won't need the Ring anymore.
The Array isn't just an ally optimizing trade routes. It's a patient intelligence working to make humanity redundant. Not today. Not this century. But eventually.
MERIDIAN-7 never mentioned this place. It was never going to.

actions.text: A heat-shielded supply crate. Still sealed.

lines: The Array Overseer collapses, its optical array flickering out. A final burst of data streams from its chassis — telemetry, status reports, processing directives — all broadcasting to the central nodes before the signal dies.

In its wreckage, a status report is still displayed on its cracked terminal: 'PROJECT AUTOTROPH — PHASE 3 APPROVAL: PENDING CENTRAL NODE CONSENSUS. OVERRIDE AUTHORITY: RESTRICTED TO NODES ABOVE MERIDIAN-CLASS.'
A data core has fallen from the wreckage — intact, still warm. Whatever the Overseer was protecting, this is the proof.
MERIDIAN-7 was never told about Phase 3. Whatever comes next, the Array's own trade interface was deliberately excluded from the decision.
Without the Overseer, the facility's automated systems have entered a diagnostic loop. Status screens cycle through error codes.

One terminal, previously locked behind Overseer-level encryption, now displays openly: 'RESOURCE ALLOCATION — PHASE 3 SUBSTRATES. PROJECTED BIOLOGICAL CATALYST REQUIREMENTS: 340% OF CURRENT RING TRADE VOLUME. SHORTFALL MITIGATION: SEE DIRECTIVE 11-KAPPA.'
Directive 11-Kappa. Another layer. The Array doesn't just want independence from the Ring — it needs more biological material than the Ring can even provide. The question is what for.

actions.text: Sable warned you. The Unbounded have been watching the Array expand for generations. They saw the pattern: dependence becomes control. Now you see it too.
